title: Under the table, the reader
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: A reader at the laundromat asks the owner if the dog is real. The owner says the dog is real; the boy is the question. Wood is in the doorway and hears it.

panels.composition: The laundromat. A READER, a woman in her sixties, with the digest at the folding table. The LAUNDRY owner.

image.prompt: a woman in her sixties reading a small photocopied booklet at a laundromat folding table while the owner stands nearby, black and white, no words
a laundromat owner folding a towel, speaking dryly, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD in the door with BARNABY. Both heard. The dog wagging; Wood not.

image.prompt: a young man and a small dog in a laundromat doorway, the dog wagging, the young man stone-faced, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The reader looking from the digest to the dog to Wood. Deciding something. Going back to the digest.

image.prompt: an older woman looking from a booklet to a small dog to a young man and back to the booklet, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'The boy's the question.' The reader decides and doesn't say.
